doc.summary: Constructs a complete TravelPath object by chaining together pre-existing paths and dynamically building new routes between nodes.
doc.overview: This function iterates through the global 'nodes' list to identify gaps in connectivity, automatically constructing missing paths using either existing connections or newly built routes. It handles various path types including portals, transports, flight paths, and teleport spells, ensuring that the resulting TravelPath is continuous from the start position to the end position.

params.name: pathToStart
params.desc: A vector of WorldPosition representing the initial segment of the path; if empty, the function begins at the first node.

params.name: pathToEnd
params.desc: A vector of WorldPosition representing the final segment of the path to be appended after processing all nodes.

params.name: bot
params.desc: An optional Unit pointer that is currently unused by this function.

doc.side_effects: Global state modification via the 'nodes' vector iteration and potential creation of new TravelNodePath objects.
doc.notes: The function relies on global 'nodes' data; callers should ensure this list is up to date. It may create temporary path objects during construction which are then integrated into the return value.

doc.summary: Constructs a new TravelNodeMap by deep copying nodes and paths from the provided base map while holding a shared lock.
doc.overview: This function initializes a new TravelNodeMap instance by iterating through every node in the input baseMap. It creates a copy of each node, replicates its path connections to other nodes, and stores these copies in the new map's internal storage. The entire operation is performed atomically by acquiring a shared lock on the base map before copying begins and releasing it immediately after completion.

params.name: baseMap
params.desc: A pointer to an existing TravelNodeMap containing the source nodes and paths to be copied.

doc.side_effects: Memory allocation (new TravelNode instances), internal state modification of the new map object.
doc.notes: The function performs a deep copy of graph topology; callers should ensure the baseMap remains valid during execution. No global state is modified.

doc.summary: Creates and registers a new TravelNode in the world, optionally checking for duplicates or auto-generating a unique name if one isn't provided.
doc.overview: This function initializes a new TravelNode instance with the specified position and properties, then adds it to the internal node list. If duplicate checking is enabled, it first attempts to retrieve an existing node at that position; otherwise, it constructs a new node using the preferred name or a generated variant if the original name conflicts with existing nodes.

params.name: pos
params.desc: The WorldPosition where the new TravelNode should be located.

params.name: preferedName
params.desc: The desired name for the TravelNode; if not important and duplicates exist, a suffix will be appended to ensure uniqueness.

params.name: isImportant
params.desc: A boolean flag indicating whether the node is marked as important, affecting how its name is handled during generation.

params.name: checkDuplicate
params.desc: If true, the function checks for an existing node at the given position and returns it immediately if found; otherwise, a new node is created.

params.name: transport
params.desc: A boolean parameter marked as maybe_unused that appears in the signature but has no effect on the logic of this function.

params.name: transportId
params.desc: An uint32 parameter marked as maybe_unused that appears in the signature but has no effect on the logic of this function.

doc.side_effects: Global state (modifies m_nodes list), I/O (regex operations)
doc.notes: Callers should be aware that if checkDuplicate is true and a node exists at pos, the new node creation is skipped. The transport parameters are present in the signature for API consistency but do not influence execution.

doc.summary: Removes a TravelNode from the internal node list and deletes its memory.
doc.overview: This function locates the specified TravelNode within the internal m_nodes vector, removes it, and then deletes the object to free its memory. It ensures that any remaining nullptr entries in the vector are cleaned up before returning.

params.name: node
params.desc: Pointer to the TravelNode instance to be removed.

doc.notes: Caller must ensure the node pointer is valid and not already deleted; passing a nullptr will result in undefined behavior due to dereferencing before the loop check.

doc.summary: Establishes bidirectional travel links between a starting node and all reachable neighboring nodes for the specified bot.
doc.overview: This function iterates through all adjacent travel nodes to create two-way paths, ensuring connectivity across the map. It skips any existing links before building new ones using the provided bot's pathfinding capabilities. Finally, it marks the start node as linked to confirm the operation's success.

params.name: startNode
params.desc: The TravelNode instance from which travel paths will be constructed.

params.name: bot
params.desc: The Unit object used to calculate and build the pathfinding data for the new links.

doc.side_effects: Network (pathfinding calculation), Global state (modifies linked status of startNode)
doc.notes: Callers must ensure the bot is active and has valid pathfinding capabilities. Edge case: If no neighboring nodes exist or all are already linked, the function completes without side effects other than setting the flag.

doc.summary: Retrieves a sorted list of nearby travel nodes within the same map as the given position.
doc.overview: This function iterates through all registered travel nodes to identify those located on the same map and within the specified distance range. The resulting vector is then sorted in ascending order based on their distance from the provided WorldPosition, ensuring that the closest nodes appear first in the output.

params.name: pos
params.desc: The WorldPosition used as the reference point for calculating distances and filtering nodes by map ID.

params.name: range
params.desc: The maximum distance in units to include; if set to -1, all nodes on the same map are included regardless of distance.

doc.notes: Callers should expect a sorted list where the first element is the closest node. The function performs no I/O or global state modifications.

doc.summary: Retrieves the nearest travel node within a specified range that is pathable to the given bot.
doc.overview: This function searches for a valid travel node starting from a specific world position and expanding outward based on the provided range. It first validates that the bot exists and has an active map, returning null if either condition fails. The search iterates through candidate nodes up to five times, prioritizing those where a path can be established between the start position and the node's location.

params.name: pos
params.desc: The world position from which travel node candidates are searched.

params.name: ppath
params.desc: An unused vector parameter intended for path storage, currently ignored by the function logic.

params.name: bot
params.desc: The unit entity whose map validity and pathability are checked against candidate nodes.

params.name: range
params.desc: The maximum distance from pos within which a valid travel node may be found.

doc.notes: Returns the first node found where `pos.canPathTo` succeeds, or null if no pathable node is discovered within five iterations or the specified range.

doc.summary: Calculates the optimal travel route between two nodes using a modified Dijkstra's algorithm that accounts for bot-specific speed, gold costs, and teleportation mechanics.
doc.overview: This function implements a pathfinding routine tailored for game bots, utilizing a priority queue to explore nodes based on estimated total cost (g + h). It dynamically adjusts the starting node's gold value based on cheat status or AI context before initiating the search. The algorithm prioritizes routes that minimize travel time while respecting movement costs and specific bot capabilities like teleportation.

params.name: start
params.desc: Pointer to the TravelNode representing the starting location for the route.

params.name: goal
params.desc: Pointer to the TravelNode representing the destination for the route.

params.name: bot
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object; if provided, the function uses bot-specific speed and gold logic, otherwise defaults to standard values.

doc.side_effects: Network (potentially via AI context), Global State (modifies sTravelNodeMap teleportNodes if a portal is created)
doc.notes: If start equals goal, it returns an empty route immediately. The function may allocate new PortalNode objects if the bot has not cast the relevant spell and a home bind exists.

doc.summary: Calculates an optimal path between two world positions by evaluating nearby travel nodes and optionally teleporting the bot to a new node if no direct route exists.
doc.overview: This function attempts to find a valid route between a starting and ending position by first checking existing travel nodes within a specific distance. If no suitable route is found among the initial set of nodes, it checks whether the bot has an active spell cooldown; if not, it teleports the bot to a new temporary node at the start position and retries the pathfinding logic.

params.name: startPos
params.desc: The starting world position for the route calculation.

params.name: endPos
params.desc: The destination world position for the route calculation.

params.name: startPath
params.desc: A reference vector containing the current path to the starting position, used to validate and update the route's start segment.

params.name: bot
params.desc: Pointer to the player bot object; if present and free from cooldowns, triggers a teleportation logic block to ensure a valid starting node exists.

doc.notes: The function relies on the bot's spell cooldown status to determine if a teleportation workaround is necessary. It modifies the global travel node map and clears the startPath vector during the fallback teleportation sequence.

doc.summary: Calculates the complete travel path between a start and end position for a bot by combining an initial segment with a route derived from the global travel node map.
doc.overview: This function first attempts to generate a direct path from the start to the end position using local pathfinding; if successful, it returns immediately. If no direct path exists, it acquires a shared lock on the global travel node map, retrieves an optimized route through the map's nodes, and constructs the final path by appending the necessary segments to connect the route to the target. The function handles optional debug logging for bot movement strategies before releasing the lock.

params.name: startPos
params.desc: The starting WorldPosition for the travel calculation.

params.name: endPos
params.desc: The destination WorldPosition for the travel calculation.

params.name: bot
params.desc: A pointer to the Player object whose AI logic determines pathfinding behavior and debug logging settings.

doc.side_effects: Locks/unlocks sTravelNodeMap, performs I/O operations (file logging) if debug strategies are active.
doc.notes: Returns an empty TravelPath if the route is deemed invalid or no path exists. Requires valid bot pointer; behavior may vary based on botAI strategy flags.

doc.summary: Removes a non-linked but unimportant TravelNode from the graph if it has fewer connected nodes than all reachable neighbors within 5000 units.
doc.overview: This function attempts to prune the travel graph by removing a specified node only if it is not currently linked and marked as unimportant. It iterates through all reachable nodes within a 5000-unit radius, comparing the number of direct connections each has; if any neighbor has more connections than the target node, removal is aborted to preserve graph integrity.

params.name: startNode
params.desc: Pointer to the TravelNode instance being evaluated for removal.

doc.returns: true if the node was successfully removed, false otherwise.
doc.side_effects: Network (modifies graph structure via removeNode), Global state (affects travel path calculations)
doc.notes: Caller must ensure startNode is not critical to current traversal; edge case occurs when all neighbors have equal or fewer connections than the target node.

doc.summary: Creates a TravelNode representing the transition between zones along all paths originating from the specified start node.
doc.overview: This function iterates through every path associated with the provided start node to identify transitions where the area name changes. For each such transition, it attempts to retrieve an existing node; if not found, it creates a new TravelNode representing the zone change and returns immediately upon success. If no zone transitions are detected across all paths, the function returns null.

params.name: startNode
params.desc: The source TravelNode whose paths will be analyzed for zone transitions.

doc.notes: Returns a pointer to the newly created node if one is added, or nullptr if no new nodes are required. The function modifies global state by potentially adding entries to sTravelNodeMap.

doc.summary: Attempts to add a random travel node connected to the specified start node by selecting from existing paths and validating connectivity.
doc.overview: This function retrieves all known paths originating from the provided start node and iterates through them up to twenty times. For each iteration, it selects a random path, checks for valid connections between nodes (including bidirectional links), and attempts to create a new travel node at a random point along that path if one does not already exist.

params.name: startNode
params.desc: Pointer to the existing TravelNode from which paths are retrieved and to which the new node must be connected.

doc.notes: Returns nullptr if no valid path is found or if all attempts fail; callers should check for null before dereferencing. Edge case: If startNode has no paths, the function immediately returns nullptr.

doc.summary: Manages travel nodes for a bot by pruning useless nodes, adding new zone or random extension nodes, and optionally printing the map based on full-map mode.
doc.overview: This function attempts to lock a shared mutex to process existing travel nodes, removing those marked as useless. It then iterates up to twenty times (or once if mapFull is true) to select a nearby node for the bot, potentially adding zone or random extension links before re-printing the map if changes were made.

params.name: bot
params.desc: Pointer to the Unit object representing the bot whose travel path is being managed.

params.name: mapFull
params.desc: Boolean flag indicating whether to limit node selection iterations to one or allow up to twenty iterations.

doc.notes: Calls cropUselessNode and addZoneLinkNode/addRandomExtNode; may trigger printMap under specific conditions. Edge case: returns early if bot has no map.

doc.summary: Generates a map of travel nodes by iterating through nearby creatures and adding specific NPC types or rank-3 entities to the global travel node registry.
doc.overview: This function scans the world for creatures within a defined radius, filtering them based on their template flags or rank. It constructs unique node names for NPCs like innkeepers and flight masters by appending role suffixes to their area name, while also registering standard rank-3 entities directly. Boss nodes are handled separately to prevent duplicate entries in the travel map.
doc.side_effects: modifies global state via sTravelNodeMap and populates the local bossMap variable
doc.notes: Relies on WorldPosition::getCreaturesNear() for input data; callers should ensure this function is invoked during appropriate world initialization or update cycles.

doc.overview: This function resets a Shadow bot to a fresh state by clearing previous data such as talents, quests, and items depending on whether an incremental update is requested. It then systematically initializes the bot's level, attributes, abilities, equipment, and consumables while logging performance metrics for each major step of the process.

doc.side_effects: Global state: Modifies bot AI configuration, performance monitoring counters, and shadow database stores. I/O: Writes debug logs.
doc.notes: Callers must ensure the bot object is valid before invoking this function. Edge case: If equipment persistence is enabled and the level exceeds the configured threshold, certain resets (talents, skills) are skipped even in non-incremental mode.

doc.notes: Callers should ensure the bot object is valid and has a corresponding PlayerInfo entry if they rely on the second loop block. Edge case: If the bot lacks the required race/class combination, only trade skills and the first two player slots are cleared.

doc.summary: Initializes a bot's talent tree by optionally incrementing the current spec, selecting a new spec via probability or template, resetting talents if requested, and distributing remaining points.
doc.overview: This function determines the target talent specification for a bot based on whether it should increment its current spec, use a predefined template, or select randomly. If incrementing is enabled, it checks specific conditions for Druids to potentially switch to the Feral cat spec; otherwise, it calculates a new spec using random probabilities defined in the configuration. After selecting the target spec, the function optionally resets the bot's talents and then applies the chosen spec along with any remaining free talent points.

params.name: increment
params.desc: If true, attempts to increment the bot's current talent specification; otherwise, selects a new specification based on probability or template.

params.name: use_template
params.desc: If true, applies a predefined talent template for the selected spec instead of distributing remaining points manually.

params.name: reset
params.desc: If true, resets the bot's current talents before applying the new configuration.

doc.side_effects: Network (SendTalentsInfoData), Global State (modifies bot talent state)
doc.notes: Calls InitTalentsByTemplate and InitTalents; edge case occurs if random selection fails to find a valid spec, defaulting to tab 0 with an error log.

doc.summary: Initializes a Shadow class bot's talent configuration based on a specific spec number and optional reset flag.
doc.overview: This function calculates the optimal talent build for a Shadow character by iterating through the game's talent store and configuration data. It first determines the starting level based on the current level and spec link order, then loops through levels to learn talents according to the defined spec path while respecting point limits. The process includes handling talent dependencies and updates the bot's internal state before sending the final talent information.

params.name: bot
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object representing the Shadow character whose talents are being configured.

params.name: specNo
params.desc: An integer identifier specifying which specific talent spec (e.g., Assassination, Outlaw) to apply.

params.name: reset
params.desc: A boolean flag; if true, forces a complete reset of the bot's existing talents before applying the new configuration.

doc.side_effects: modifies global talent store lookups, updates bot state (talents learned, free points), and triggers network I/O via SendTalentsInfoData
doc.notes: Callers must ensure the bot object is valid and has sufficient free talent points if not resetting. Edge case: If the spec link order for a level is empty or the bot runs out of points before reaching max level, the function exits early without learning all intended talents.

doc.summary: Initializes a player's talents based on a parsed spec link, optionally resetting them first.
doc.overview: This function populates the specified player with talents according to the provided spec link structure. It iterates through the talent store to build a mapping of rows to their corresponding entries, filtering by class mask and tab page. For each entry in the parsed spec link, it resolves dependencies and learns the talent while tracking free points until exhaustion.

params.name: bot
params.desc: Pointer to the player object whose talents are being configured.

params.name: parsedSpecLink
params.desc: A vector of vectors containing the talent specification data, where each inner vector represents a specific talent entry with tab, row, column, and level indices.

params.name: reset
params.desc: Boolean flag indicating whether to clear the player's current talents before applying the new spec.

doc.notes: Calls bot->LearnTalent which may trigger dependency chains; breaks early if free talent points are depleted.

doc.summary: Destroys items in a player's inventory that are not marked for keeping, using a visitor pattern to iterate through items.
doc.overview: The DestroyItemsVisitor class extends IterateItemsVisitor to selectively remove items from a bot's inventory based on a configurable keep list. It iterates through each item, checks if the item's ID is in the 'keep' set or matches a random quest item list, and destroys the item only if it should not be retained. The visitor pattern allows for flexible iteration logic while encapsulating the specific destruction behavior.
doc.notes: Callers must ensure the 'keep' set is populated before invoking this visitor. Edge case: If an item's ID matches both the keep list and a random quest item, it will be kept due to the order of checks in CanKeep().

doc.summary: Verifies whether a bot can equip a specific armor item template by checking if the required skill for that armor type is present.
doc.overview: This function iterates through the armor subclass of the provided item template and compares it against the bot's current skill set. It returns false immediately if the item requires a skill the bot does not possess, such as Plate Mail requiring SKILL_PLATE_MAIL or Leather requiring SKILL_LEATHER. If the item type matches one of the supported armor categories and the corresponding skill is available, the function proceeds to return true.

params.name: proto
params.desc: Pointer to an ItemTemplate object containing details about the armor item, specifically its SubClass field.

doc.notes: The function relies on global bot state via the 'bot' pointer to check skill availability. It does not perform any I/O or modify global configuration.

doc.summary: Validates whether a bot's class is compatible with the provided spell points, attack points, and tank requirements.
doc.overview: This function checks if a specific bot class meets the resource constraints defined by sp (spell points), ap (attack points), and tank (tank points). It returns false immediately if the bot lacks the required resources or if the resource distribution violates class-specific logic, such as requiring both attack and tank points for certain classes. If all conditions are satisfied, it returns true.

params.name: sp
params.desc: The number of spell points available.

params.name: ap
params.desc: The number of attack points available.

params.name: tank
params.desc: The number of tank points available.

doc.notes: Returns true only if at least one resource (sp, ap, or tank) is present; otherwise returns false even if the class checks pass. Callers should ensure bot->getClass() is valid before invoking.

doc.summary: Increments the specified stat counters for a given item modification type.
doc.overview: This function updates three shared stat pools (spirit, agility, and power) based on the item's modification category. It uses separate switch statements to determine which counters to increment, ensuring that specific mods like Health or Stamina affect multiple stats while others like Intellect only affect Spirit.

params.name: mod
params.desc: The type of item modification (e.g., HEALTH, STRENGTH, AGILITY) determining which stats to increment.

params.name: sp
params.desc: A reference to the spirit stat counter that is incremented if the mod matches specific categories.

params.name: ap
params.desc: A reference to the agility/power stat counter that is incremented for a broader range of mods including physical and mental attributes.

params.name: tank
params.desc: A reference to the tank stat counter, which aggregates stats related to health, stamina, strength, and agility.

doc.notes: The function modifies the state of the sp, ap, and tank references directly. It does not perform I/O or access global state outside of these local variables.

doc.summary: Determines if a specific weapon template is valid for equipping by a given bot class based on its subclass type.
doc.overview: This function iterates through the available classes in the game, checking each one against the provided item template to verify compatibility. It returns false immediately if the bot's class does not match any of the predefined cases or if the weapon's subclass is not permitted for that class. If all checks pass without returning false, the function concludes that the weapon can be equipped and returns true.

params.name: proto
params.desc: Pointer to an ItemTemplate object containing the weapon's subclass information.

doc.notes: The function relies on the bot object being accessible within the current scope, as it references 'bot->getClass()'. It performs no I/O or network operations and does not modify global state.

doc.summary: Determines whether a specific item template can be equipped by the current bot instance based on duration, bonding type, class, inventory count, and level requirements.
doc.overview: This function evaluates multiple constraints to decide if an item is eligible for equipping. It first checks that the item does not have a duration set and is not bound to a quest, then verifies the item's class and whether the bot possesses at least one instance of it. Finally, it ensures the bot meets the minimum level requirement before returning true.

params.name: proto
params.desc: Pointer to the ItemTemplate structure containing metadata such as duration, bonding type, class, required level, and item ID.

doc.notes: The function relies on external state via bot->HasItemCount() and bot->GetLevel(), meaning it assumes the bot object is valid and initialized. It returns false if the item has a duration or is quest-bound, regardless of other conditions.

doc.summary: Shuffles the contents of a vector in place using a custom loop-based algorithm.
doc.overview: This function performs an in-place shuffle on the provided vector by repeatedly swapping two randomly selected elements. It iterates a fixed number of times (five times the vector size) rather than using standard Fisher-Yates, which may result in less statistically uniform randomness compared to optimized implementations. The operation modifies the original container directly without returning any data.

params.name: items
params.desc: The vector containing uint32 elements to be shuffled; modified in place.

doc.notes: Callers should expect the order of elements to change unpredictably. Edge case: if items is empty, the loop condition fails immediately and no operation occurs.

doc.summary: Initializes equipment for Shadow AI bots by either equipping starting outfits or procedurally generating gear based on level and configuration flags.
doc.overview: This function configures a bot's inventory by first checking if it should use incremental gear initialization; if so, it equips items from the character's starting outfit while skipping consumables and duplicates. For higher levels, it iterates through equipment slots to either remove existing items (if second_chance is enabled) or replace them with procedurally generated items that match level requirements, quality settings, and specific exclusion rules.

params.name: incremental
params.desc: If true, the function attempts to equip items from the bot's starting outfit rather than generating new gear.

params.name: second_chance
params.desc: If true, existing items in equipment slots are destroyed before attempting to equip new ones.

doc.side_effects: Modifies bot inventory (adding or removing items), performs I/O operations via item storage and retrieval.
doc.notes: Calls GetCharStartOutfitEntry, StoreNewItemInBestSlots, and various slot-specific checks; skips specific item IDs like 6948 and 46978; respects gear score limits and expansion restrictions defined in sShadowAIConfig.

doc.summary: Determines if a specific item should be replaced based on the bot's current level and the item's template requirements.
doc.overview: This function evaluates whether an item qualifies for replacement by checking its quality tier against a rarity threshold and comparing its required level to the bot's current level. It calculates a dynamic delta factor that increases as the bot's level decreases relative to the item's requirement, using this value to decide if the item is too low quality or too high level for the bot.

params.name: item
params.desc: Pointer to the Item instance being evaluated for replacement.

doc.notes: The function relies on external state accessed via bot->GetLevel() and item->GetTemplate(). Returns true if the item is null, has no required level, or fails the quality/level comparison logic.

doc.summary: Attempts to store a new item into the player's bag inventory and returns the resulting item pointer if successful.
doc.overview: This function checks if the player can accept a new item into their primary bag slot (INVENTORY_SLOT_BAG_0) using the CanStoreNewItem method. If the storage operation succeeds, it calls StoreNewItem to actually place the item in the inventory with randomized properties generated from the provided ID. The function returns the newly stored Item pointer on success or nullptr if the player cannot store the item.

params.name: player
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object attempting to store the item.

params.name: newItemId
params.desc: The unique identifier for the new item to be stored.

params.name: count
params.desc: The quantity of the item to attempt to store.

doc.notes: Callers should check for nullptr before using the returned pointer. Edge case: If the player has no space in INVENTORY_SLOT_BAG_0 or cannot store the specific item type, nullptr is returned.

doc.summary: InitBags populates the player's inventory bag slots with a specific item ID (51809) while optionally destroying existing items of that same ID.
doc.overview: This function iterates through all available bag slots to equip a predefined item, skipping any slot already occupied by an identical item. When the destroyOld flag is enabled, it actively removes existing items from the target slot before equipping the new one; otherwise, it simply skips occupied slots. The logic ensures that only unique instances of the item are added to the inventory.

params.name: destroyOld
params.desc: A boolean flag indicating whether existing items in the target slot should be destroyed before equipping the new item.

doc.notes: The function modifies the bot's inventory directly. It relies on internal helper functions like GetItemByPos and CanEquipUnseenItem which may have side effects or depend on game state.

doc.summary: Attempts to apply a random permanent enchantment to the specified item if the executing bot meets level and gear requirements.
doc.overview: This function checks whether the current bot has sufficient level and a low enough gear score to perform an enchantment. It iterates through all available spells to find those that can enchant the target item, filtering by spell level, item level, and specific enchantment effects. If valid enchantments are found, one is selected at random and applied permanently to the item.

params.name: item
params.desc: Pointer to the Item object that will be enchanted.

doc.notes: Requires bot->GetLevel() and access to sShadowAIConfig, sSpellMgr, and sSpellItemEnchantmentStore. May log debug messages if no enchantments are found.

doc.summary: Attempts to create a temporary item instance and check if it can be equipped into the specified slot, returning true only on successful equip.
doc.overview: This function creates a new item instance from the provided ID and immediately attempts to equip it into the target slot using either the bot AI or the main bot's logic. If the item creation fails or the equip check returns an error, the function cleans up the temporary object and returns false; otherwise, it returns true upon success.

params.name: slot
params.desc: The inventory slot index where the unseen item is being attempted to be equipped.

params.name: dest
params.desc: A reference variable that will store the destination slot if the item cannot be equipped directly (e.g., due to full inventory).

params.name: item
params.desc: The unique identifier of the unseen item to be created and tested for equipability.

doc.side_effects: Item creation, potential bot AI invocation, inventory state modification, memory allocation/deallocation
doc.notes: Callers should expect a false return if the item cannot be equipped or does not exist; the dest parameter is only populated on failure. Edge case: If Item::CreateItem fails, no temporary object is created and dest remains unchanged.

doc.summary: Initializes a bot's trade skills by retrieving or generating class-specific skill pairs and setting random utility skills.
doc.overview: This function attempts to retrieve pre-defined first and second trade skills for a given bot; if they are missing, it generates them based on the bot's class or randomly selects from a predefined set. After establishing these primary skills, it unconditionally assigns four additional utility skills (First Aid, Fishing, Cooking, and one of the generated pair) to ensure the bot has a balanced skillset.
doc.side_effects: Global state: Modifies sRandomShadowMgr values for firstSkill and secondSkill; Sets random skills via SetRandomSkill calls.
doc.notes: Callers should ensure the bot object is valid before invoking. Edge case: If a class has no predefined skill list, it defaults to Tailoring and Enchanting.

For most attributes, it adds the provided value directly, but mana and health regeneration values are scaled down by dividing them by 10 and 15 respectively. Additionally, certain hit and critical rating modifiers only contribute to the stats if the collector's type flag matches the specific attack style (melee, ranged, or spell).

params.desc: The specific item modification type being processed, such as MANA_REGENERATION, HIT_MELEE_RATING, or ATTACK_POWER.

params.name: val
params.desc: The integer value representing the magnitude of the stat modification to be added.

doc.notes: Callers must ensure the collector type is set correctly before invoking this function for hit/crit modifiers. Edge case: if an invalid itemStatType is passed, no operation occurs.

doc.summary: Calculates and accumulates various stat values based on the specified spell aura effect, multiplier, and trigger conditions.
doc.overview: This function processes spell effects to update internal statistics by evaluating the effect type against a series of specific cases. It determines the base value using an average calculation and applies the provided multiplier to adjust the final stat increments. The logic includes conditional checks for school types, combat ratings, and specific stat categories to ensure accurate data collection.

params.name: effectInfo
params.desc: A SpellEffectInfo struct containing details about the spell effect, including its name, type, and miscellaneous values used for calculations.

params.name: multiplier
params.desc: A float value representing the scaling factor applied to the calculated base value before updating stats.

params.name: canNextTrigger
params.desc: A boolean flag indicating whether the next trigger is allowed, though its usage within the function body is not explicitly shown in the provided snippet.

params.name: triggerCooldown
params.desc: An unsigned 32-bit integer representing a cooldown period for the trigger mechanism.

doc.notes: The function relies on global variables such as 'stats', 'type_', and 'CollectorType' which must be properly initialized. It performs bitwise operations on school masks and combat ratings, requiring careful handling of bit flags. The logic for specific cases like SPELL_AURA_MOD_STAT includes a default case that applies all five primary stats when the stat type is -1.

doc.summary: Calculates the average value of a spell effect by adding a randomized bonus based on the number of die sides.
doc.overview: This function determines the total points for a spell effect by starting with its base points and applying a conditional randomization. If the effect has no dice (0 sides), it returns the base points unchanged. For one die, it adds exactly one point to the base value. Any other number of dice results in an average bonus calculated as half the number of sides plus 0.5.

params.name: effectInfo
params.desc: A reference to the spell effect information containing BasePoints and DieSides.

doc.notes: The function performs no I/O, network operations, or global state modifications. It is safe for use in high-frequency game loops.

doc.summary: Validates whether a collected spell instance matches the expected class, family, type, and flag constraints.
doc.overview: This function performs strict validation on spell data by comparing the internal class and spell family against provided parameters. It specifically checks for healing spells when in strict mode or ensures non-healing spells are not flagged as such. Additionally, it enforces specific casting flags for Druids, Paladins, and Shamans based on their class type and spell category.

params.name: spellFamilyName
params.desc: The expected spell family identifier to validate against the collected instance.

params.name: spelFalimyFlags
params.desc: A flag set used to verify casting restrictions, particularly for specific classes like Druids and Paladins.

params.name: strict
params.desc: A boolean indicating whether the function should enforce strict healing spell validation rules.

doc.notes: The function relies on global ShadowAI state for class and spell family identification. It returns false if any specific class-flag combination (Druid, Paladin, Shaman) violates the provided flag constraints.

doc.summary: Calculates the final statistical weight for a specific item by aggregating base stats, random properties, overflow penalties, and various modifiers.
doc.overview: This function retrieves the item template from the global store and initializes internal state before collecting raw statistics. It conditionally processes random properties if provided, applies an overflow penalty to the player, and aggregates weighted stats across all types. The final weight is computed by summing individual stat contributions and applying additional modifiers for item sets, sockets, and quality-based gear scores.

params.name: itemId
params.desc: The unique identifier of the item to calculate statistics for.

params.name: randomPropertyIds
params.desc: An array of property IDs representing random properties to be calculated; if zero, this step is skipped.

doc.side_effects: Global state (item template lookup), internal state reset and collection via collector_, potential player state modification for overflow penalties and item set bonuses.
doc.notes: Returns early with 0.0f if the itemId is invalid or not found in the store. The function relies on global object manager access and modifies internal weight accumulators before returning.

doc.summary: Calculates the total enchant weight for a player by aggregating collected statistics and applying overflow penalties.
doc.overview: This function retrieves an enchantment entry from the global store using the provided ID, returning zero if the enchantment is not found. It initializes internal state, collects current enchant stats, applies any configured overflow penalties to the player, and computes the final weight by summing weighted statistics across all types.

params.name: enchantId
params.desc: The unique identifier for the enchantment entry to look up in the spell item enchantment store.

doc.side_effects: Global state (lookup), I/O (collector interaction), and potential global state modification (overflow penalty application).
doc.notes: Callers must ensure the enchantId is valid to avoid unnecessary lookups; edge case occurs when the enchantment does not exist, resulting in a return value of 0.0f.

doc.summary: Calculates and collects statistics for random properties of an item based on a specific property ID or suffix.
doc.overview: This function determines whether to process random enchantments or random suffixes by checking the sign of the provided randomPropertyId. It retrieves the corresponding entry from either the ItemRandomPropertiesStore or ItemRandomSuffixStore, then iterates through all possible enchantment slots to look up and collect associated spell item enchantment statistics.

params.name: randomPropertyId
params.desc: The ID of the random property entry; if positive, it refers to a standard random property, while if negative, it refers to a random suffix.

params.name: itemId
params.desc: The unique identifier of the item for which enchantment statistics are being calculated.

doc.notes: Caller must ensure randomPropertyId is valid; returns early if the lookup fails. Edge case: negative IDs are treated as suffixes by negating them before lookup.

doc.summary: Generates a complete weight profile for a specific player by combining basic, additional, and fine-tuned calculations.
doc.overview: This function orchestrates the calculation of statistical weights for a given player instance by sequentially invoking three specialized sub-routines. It first establishes foundational values through GenerateBasicWeights, augments them with context-specific data via GenerateAdditionalWeights, and finally applies custom adjustments using ApplyWeightFinetune to produce the final result.

params.name: player
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object for which weights are being calculated.

doc.notes: The function assumes all three internal helper functions (GenerateBasicWeights, GenerateAdditionalWeights, ApplyWeightFinetune) are defined and accessible within the same translation unit or header. Ensure the Player object is fully initialized before calling this function to avoid undefined behavior.

doc.summary: Calculates and applies base stat weights for a player based on their class, specialization tab, and specific role requirements.
doc.overview: This function initializes the internal stats weight map by adding default values for all stat types. It then iterates through conditional blocks to apply specialized multipliers for specific classes like Hunter, Rogue, Druid, Warrior, and Death Knight depending on their chosen playstyle or specialization tab. The logic includes a runtime check for Shadow AI tanks within the Druid class to adjust weights accordingly.

params.name: player
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object containing the class identifier (cls) and current specialization tab.

doc.side_effects: Modifies internal state via stats_weights_ map; performs no I/O or network operations.
doc.notes: The function relies on global constants for stat types, classes, and tabs. Callers must ensure the player object is valid before invocation. Edge case: The Druid Feral branch explicitly excludes Shadow AI tanks to prevent inappropriate weight application.

doc.summary: Calculates additional stat weights for a player based on their class and active auras.
doc.overview: This function determines bonus stat multipliers by first identifying the player's class, then checking for specific active auras associated with that class. If matching conditions are met, it increments the corresponding entry in the stats_weights_ map with a predefined float value.

params.name: player
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object whose stat weights are being calculated.

doc.notes: Modifies the internal stats_weights_ map; callers should ensure this map is accessible or passed as a reference if used elsewhere. Edge case: If the player's class does not match Hunter, Warrior, or Shaman, no weights are added.

doc.summary: Calculates the item set bonus multiplier for a specific item set based on the current equipped items and applies it to the global weight.
doc.overview: This function determines a multiplicative factor by iterating through the player's active item set effects to find matches with the provided item template. It calculates the multiplier based on how many items from the set are currently equipped, capping the bonus at full completion or applying a default bonus if no specific match is found.

params.name: player
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object containing the active item set effects.

params.name: proto
params.desc: Const pointer to the ItemTemplate defining the target item set ID and its requirements.

doc.side_effects: Global state modification via weight_ multiplication.
doc.notes: The function modifies the global variable 'weight_' by multiplying it with the calculated multiplier. It relies on the sItemSetStore lookup and assumes player->ItemSetEff is populated correctly.

doc.summary: Calculates the socket bonus multiplier for an item by counting colored gem sockets and applying a linear increase to the item's weight.
doc.overview: This function iterates through the gem socket array of an ItemTemplate to count how many sockets contain a valid color. It then computes a multiplicative factor based on this count, adding 3% per socket to a base value of 1.0, and finally applies this multiplier to the global weight_ variable.

params.name: player
params.desc: The player object associated with the item; currently unused.

params.name: proto
params.desc: A pointer to the ItemTemplate structure containing the gem socket color data.

doc.side_effects: Modifies global state by updating weight_ with the calculated socket bonus multiplier.
doc.notes: The player parameter is marked as [[maybe_unused]] and has no effect on the calculation. The function relies on the ItemTemplate's Socket array being populated correctly.

doc.summary: Calculates the final item weight penalty by applying class-specific multipliers based on weapon type, subclass, player abilities, and active auras.
doc.overview: This function modifies an internal weight accumulator to reflect how different character classes interact with specific weapon types. It applies reduction multipliers for double-handed weapons or single-handed weapons favored by certain classes, while increasing the weight for items that are less desirable due to lack of dual-wielding capability or specific subclass restrictions. The logic also includes conditional bonuses for high-level rogue daggers and players possessing specific auras.

params.name: proto
params.desc: Pointer to the ItemTemplate structure containing details such as Class, SubClass, and Delay.

doc.notes: Modifies the external variable weight_; Requires access to player state via player_ for ability checks and aura detection; Logic is heavily dependent on specific class tab configurations.

It iterates through three primary armor types—Plate Mail, Mail, and Leather—and checks if the player possesses the corresponding skill to determine validity. If no matching skill is found, the function defaults to returning false, indicating no conflict.

params.name: item_subclass_armor
params.desc: The armor subclass of the item being evaluated (e.g., ITEM_SUBCLASS_ARMOR_PLATE).

doc.notes: Callers should ensure the player object is valid before invoking this function to avoid null pointer dereferences. Edge cases include players with no armor skills, which will always return false regardless of the item type.

doc.summary: Calculates and caps the overflow values for hit chance, expertise, defense skill, and armor penetration based on a player's current stats and rating bonuses.
doc.overview: This function determines the maximum possible stat value (overflow) for four specific categories: spell/melee hit chance, expertise, defense skill, and armor penetration. It compares these theoretical overflows against the player's existing values to calculate any excess points available. The calculated overflow amounts are then stored in a collector's stats dictionary, ensuring that the recorded values never exceed the previously stored maximums.

params.name: player
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object containing current stat values and rating bonuses.

doc.notes: Modifies the state of `collector_->stats` by updating or capping existing entries for STATS_TYPE_HIT, STATS_TYPE_EXPERTISE, STATS_TYPE_DEFENSE, and STATS_TYPE_ARMOR_PENETRATION.

doc.summary: Applies a 20% weight increase to armor penetration for players with high rating bonuses when equipped with melee or ranged collectors.
doc.overview: This function checks if the player has any active collector types (melee or ranged) and evaluates their armor penetration rating bonus. If the bonus exceeds 50, it multiplies the internal stats weight for armor penetration by 1.2 to reflect increased importance in the game's balancing system.

params.name: player
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object whose equipment and rating bonuses are being evaluated.

doc.notes: The function relies on internal state (stats_weights_) which is not visible here; callers must ensure the StatsWeightCalculator instance is valid. Edge case: if armor penetration bonus is exactly 50, no modification occurs.

It performs deep copies of each action object to ensure the resulting list is independent of the originals, then explicitly deallocates the memory used by the input lists before returning the new combined list.

doc.summary: BuildSharedTriggerContexts populates a shared object list with all standard and raid-specific trigger contexts used by the AI system.
doc.overview: This function serves as a factory method that initializes the global set of trigger contexts available to the game's artificial intelligence. It iterates through a hardcoded collection of context types, ranging from basic chat interactions to numerous World of Warcraft raid instances across different expansions, and adds them sequentially to the provided list. By centralizing this initialization in a single call, the AI system ensures consistent access to all necessary trigger data without requiring individual instantiation logic elsewhere.

params.desc: A reference to a SharedNamedObjectContextList that will be populated with new TriggerContext instances.

doc.notes: The function does not take any input arguments other than the destination list; all context types are added unconditionally. Callers should ensure the target list has sufficient capacity before invoking this function to prevent potential memory issues.

doc.side_effects: Memory allocation for new object; modification of external list state.

doc.summary: Serializes all created value contexts in the object context into a vector of formatted strings.

doc.notes: The caller should expect that the returned vector may be empty if no value contexts have been created or if all values serialize to the marker '?'. This function relies on internal state managed by GetCreated() and GetUntypedValue().

doc.notes: Callers should ensure the provided name exists in the context to avoid unexpected empty returns; useful for grouping strategies by shared configuration or parent node.

doc.summary: Retrieves a specific AI context object by its name from the global trigger registry.

It delegates the lookup operation to the internal TriggerContexts manager, ensuring thread-safe retrieval of bot-specific AI configurations. The returned pointer is valid only while the corresponding trigger remains registered and active.

params.name: name

If two non-empty tokens are provided, the first becomes the action name and the second is converted to a float value; otherwise, if only one token exists, it defaults to ACTION_NORMAL. Invalid inputs trigger an error log before returning null.

doc.summary: Converts a comma-separated string of action names into a dynamically allocated array of NextAction pointers.

params.name: actionLine
params.desc: The input string containing the action definition, expected to be formatted as 'action>next_actions'.

doc.notes: Returns nullptr if the input does not contain exactly two parts separated by '>' or if the format is invalid. The caller must check for null before using the returned pointer.

doc.summary: Executes a sequence of action execution listeners to determine if an action should proceed based on their individual results.
doc.overview: This function iterates through all registered ActionExecutionListener objects and invokes the Before method on each one, passing the current action and event. The overall result is true only if every listener returns true, effectively acting as a logical AND across all listeners. If any listener returns false, the function immediately stops further iteration and returns false to prevent the action from executing.

params.name: action
params.desc: Pointer to the Action object being evaluated.

params.name: event
params.desc: The Event object associated with the current game state or action context.

doc.notes: Callers should ensure that listeners are properly registered in the Engine before invoking this function. Edge case: if the listeners list is empty, the function returns true immediately without executing any logic.

doc.summary: Invokes the After callback on all registered ActionExecutionListeners after an action has been processed.
doc.overview: This function iterates through a list of registered listeners and calls their After method to notify them that an action execution is complete. It serves as the central dispatch mechanism for post-execution logic within the strategy engine, ensuring every component subscribed to this event receives the necessary context about the action and its execution status.

params.name: action
params.desc: Pointer to the Action object that was just executed.

params.name: executed
params.desc: Boolean flag indicating whether the action was successfully executed.

params.name: event
params.desc: The Event object associated with this action execution.

doc.notes: Callers must ensure the listeners list is populated before invoking this function; passing a null pointer for 'action' may cause undefined behavior if listener implementations do not handle it gracefully.

doc.summary: Overrides the execution result of an action by propagating a decision through a chain of listeners.
doc.overview: This function determines whether an action should be executed by first checking if it has already been executed, then iterating through registered listeners to see if any override this decision. The initial result is set based on the 'executed' flag, and each listener in the chain receives the current result to potentially modify it before returning the final outcome.

params.name: action
params.desc: Pointer to the Action object being evaluated.

params.name: executed
params.desc: Boolean flag indicating whether the action has already been executed.

params.name: event
params.desc: The Event associated with this action execution.

doc.notes: Callers should ensure the 'listeners' list is properly initialized before invoking this function. Edge case: if no listeners are registered, the function simply returns the value of the 'executed' parameter.

doc.summary: Allows execution of an action by checking if all registered listeners permit it.
doc.overview: This function iterates through a list of ActionExecutionListener objects and aggregates their individual AllowExecution results using logical AND. It returns true only if every listener grants permission, effectively acting as a gatekeeper for action execution within the strategy engine.

params.name: action
params.desc: Pointer to the Action object being evaluated for execution.

params.name: event
params.desc: The Event context associated with the action's execution attempt.

doc.notes: Callers should ensure the 'listeners' list is not empty before relying on this function for critical game logic. If any listener returns false, the entire operation is blocked regardless of other listeners.

doc.overview: This destructor iterates through the stored ActionExecutionListener objects, deleting each one to free their memory. After ensuring all individual listeners are destroyed, it empties the listeners container to prevent any dangling references or resource leaks.
doc.side_effects: Memory deallocation for listener objects and clearing of internal state.
doc.notes: Callers should ensure this is called when the Engine object goes out of scope; no edge cases exist as it simply performs cleanup.

doc.summary: Executes the AI decision-making loop for a unit by processing triggers, evaluating actions based on relevance and prerequisites, and returning whether any action was successfully performed.
doc.overview: This function initiates the core AI tick cycle by clearing stale actions from the queue and logging configuration values if enabled. It iterates through available actions, adjusting their relevance scores using multipliers and checking for prerequisite conditions before execution. The loop terminates once a valid action is executed or the iteration limit is reached, ensuring the unit performs one decisive move per tick.

params.name: unit
params.desc: Pointer to the Unit object; currently unused by this function.

params.name: depth
params.desc: Integer depth value for recursion or search hierarchy; currently unused by this function.

params.name: minimal
params.desc: Boolean flag indicating whether to prioritize high-relevance actions only, skipping low-scoring options.

doc.side_effects: I/O (logging), Network (action execution via ListenAndExecute), Global State (modifies queue and action relevance scores)
doc.notes: Callers must ensure the unit is active before invoking. Edge case: if no actions are possible or relevant, the function returns false without modifying global state beyond logging.

doc.summary: Creates or retrieves an ActionNode instance using a name as the key in the action node factory registry.
doc.overview: This function attempts to fetch an existing ActionNode from the global actionNodeFactories registry using the provided name. If no node exists for that name, it constructs and returns a new ActionNode with null children and parent references.

params.name: name
params.desc: The unique identifier string used to look up or create an ActionNode in the factory registry.

doc.side_effects: Global state (modifies actionNodeFactories if a new node is created)
doc.notes: Callers should check for null return values only if they expect the function to fail, though this implementation always returns a valid pointer. Edge case: If the name already exists in the registry, the existing node is returned without modification.

doc.summary: Creates and queues ActionNode instances from a provided array of NextAction pointers, optionally overriding relevance values before pushing to the action queue.
doc.overview: This function iterates through an array of NextAction objects, constructs corresponding ActionNode instances, and conditionally pushes them into the global action queue. It supports dynamic relevance adjustment via forceRelevance and respects skipPrerequisites settings when queuing. The function returns true if at least one action was successfully queued.

params.name: actions
params.desc: Pointer to an array of NextAction objects; the loop terminates when a null pointer is encountered.

params.name: forceRelevance
params.desc: Float value that overrides the relevance score of actions if greater than zero.

params.name: skipPrerequisites
params.desc: Boolean flag indicating whether prerequisite checks should be skipped when queuing actions.

params.name: event
params.desc: Event type associated with the pushed action basket.

params.name: pushType
params.desc: String identifier describing the type of push operation being performed.

doc.side_effects: Global state: modifies the action queue; I/O: writes log messages.
doc.notes: Caller must ensure actions array is null-terminated and owns the memory for all NextAction elements to be deleted. Edge case: if forceRelevance is set but results in k <= 0, the action is created but not queued and immediately deleted.

doc.summary: Executes a specified game action by creating the necessary node and object, applying optional qualifiers, validating feasibility, and returning the execution result.
doc.overview: This function initializes an action based on its name and event type, optionally applying a qualifier if provided. It performs critical validation checks to ensure the action is both possible and useful before proceeding to listen for events and execute the logic. Finally, it handles cleanup by deleting the temporary action node and returns a status indicating success or failure.

params.name: name
params.desc: The identifier string used to locate and instantiate the specific ActionNode.

params.name: event
params.desc: The game event that triggers the execution of the action.

params.name: qualifier
params.desc: An optional string used to modify or qualify the behavior of the action if it is a Qualified type.

doc.side_effects: Memory allocation for ActionNode and Action objects; potential dynamic_cast failure; deletion of temporary objects; I/O via ListenAndExecute.
doc.notes: Callers must ensure the action name corresponds to a registered strategy. Edge cases include actions that are impossible or useless, which result in early termination and resource cleanup.

doc.summary: Adds a new AI strategy to the engine's registry and optionally initializes it.
doc.overview: This function registers a strategy by name in the global context, automatically removing any existing strategy with the same name. If an existing strategy is found, its siblings are also removed before the new instance is added to the strategies map. The function then conditionally calls the strategy's initialization routine if the init flag is set.

params.name: name
params.desc: The unique identifier string for the strategy to be added.

params.name: init
params.desc: A boolean flag indicating whether to immediately initialize the strategy upon registration.

doc.side_effects: Global state (modifies aiObjectContext and strategies map); I/O (calls LogAction)
doc.notes: Callers must ensure 'name' is valid; if a strategy with this name already exists, it will be replaced rather than coexisting.

doc.summary: Registers a list of strategy names with the engine and initializes the system.

params.desc: The first strategy name to register.

doc.side_effects: Global state (strategy registry), I/O (potential logging via Init)
doc.notes: Callers should ensure all arguments are valid non-empty strings; the function relies on va_arg for variable argument list processing.

params.desc: The first strategy name to register.

doc.side_effects: Global state (modifies the internal strategy registry)
doc.notes: Callers should ensure all provided strings are valid strategy names; passing null or empty strings may result in undefined behavior depending on addStrategy's implementation.

doc.side_effects: modifies global strategies map, calls LogAction and potentially Init()
doc.notes: Returns false if the strategy name is not found; callers should verify this before assuming successful removal.

doc.summary: A templated base class for ShadowAI bots that provides a thread-safe, interval-based mechanism to retrieve or update calculated values.
doc.overview: CalculatedValue serves as the foundational template class for bot strategies in the game server, inheriting from both UntypedValue and Value<T>. It implements a configurable polling system where the checkInterval parameter determines how frequently the underlying Calculate() function is invoked. The class supports three retrieval modes: Get() performs a full recalculation on every call if the interval is set to 1, otherwise it checks against the last execution time; LazyGet() returns the cached value immediately unless it has never been computed; and RefGet() allows direct access to the current value while respecting the same interval logic.
doc.notes: The checkInterval parameter is automatically scaled: values of 1 remain 1, values between 2 and 99 are multiplied by 1000 (milliseconds), and values >= 100 are treated as seconds. The protected Calculate() function must be overridden by derived classes to define the specific logic for generating the value.

params.desc: Pointer to a SpellInfo structure containing the spell ID, localized name, and optional rank data.

It then iterates through the spell's effects to identify any additional spells that should be learned as part of this action, learning them only if they are not already known by the bot. Finally, it checks if the primary spell itself needs to be learned and executes that action if necessary.

params.desc: The ID of the spell to attempt to learn.

doc.notes: The function relies on the bot object being valid and accessible. It may learn multiple spells if the primary spell's effects include other SPELL_EFFECT_LEARN_SPELL triggers.

Once a valid banker is found, it delegates the actual banking operation to ExecuteBank, passing the transaction text and the target NPC's GUID. If no suitable banker exists within range, an error message is logged and the function returns false.

params.name: event
params.desc: The event object containing the action parameters, specifically the transaction text.

doc.notes: Relies on botAI->GetUnit and UNIT_NPC_FLAG_BANKER for NPC identification; callers must ensure the event contains a valid 'text' parameter.

doc.summary: Executes bank-related commands by parsing text input to either list items, withdraw specific items, or deposit items into the bank.
doc.overview: This function processes a string command to interact with a unit's bank. If the text is empty or contains only '?', it lists all items in the bank and returns true. For other inputs, it checks the first character: a '-' prefix triggers item withdrawal by parsing the remaining text against items currently in the bank, while any other character attempts to deposit items found in bags matching the text.

params.name: text
params.desc: The command string; empty or '?' lists items, '-' prefixed strings withdraw items, otherwise deposits items from bags.

params.name: bank
params.desc: Pointer to the Unit object representing the bank (marked as maybe_unused).

doc.notes: Returns true only if all operations succeed; returns false on empty input, missing items for withdrawal, or failure to find items for deposit.

doc.summary: Withdraws a specified item from the player's bank inventory and stores it in their main inventory.
doc.overview: This function attempts to locate an item with the given ID in the bank. If found, it checks if the bot can store the item in its current inventory configuration; if storage fails, it sends an error message and returns false. Upon successful storage, the item is removed from the bank and added to the inventory, followed by a notification sent to the master.

params.name: itemid
params.desc: The unique identifier of the item to withdraw from the bank.

doc.side_effects: Inventory modification, network communication (error messages and master notifications)
doc.notes: Returns false if the item is not found in the bank or if the bot cannot store it in its inventory.

doc.summary: Deposits a specified item into the bot's bank inventory after verifying it can be stored.
doc.overview: This function attempts to deposit an item into the bot's bank by first checking if the destination slot is valid and available. If the item cannot be deposited, it sends an error message to the master and returns false; otherwise, it removes the item from its current location, places it in the bank, and logs the successful transaction.

params.name: pItem
params.desc: Pointer to the Item instance that is intended to be deposited into the bank.

doc.side_effects: Inventory modification, network communication (error or success message)
doc.notes: Caller must ensure pItem is not null. Returns false if the bot cannot accept the item into the bank.

It then checks the bot's level against the battleground template to ensure it meets the minimum access requirements for that specific battleground. Finally, it calculates the required bracket ID based on the map and the bot's level, comparing it against the provided bracketId to confirm a match.

params.name: queueTypeId
params.desc: The type of battleground queue the bot is attempting to join.

params.name: bracketId
params.desc: The specific bracket ID the bot is trying to enter within the battleground.

doc.notes: Returns false if the bot is already in a queue of this type, lacks level access for the battleground, or the calculated bracket does not match the requested bracketId.

Finally, it assesses availability based on team affiliation (Alliance or Horde) for non-arena battlegrounds.

params.desc: The unique identifier for the Battleground queue type.

params.name: bracketId
params.desc: The specific bracket or instance ID within the queue.

doc.notes: Reads from global managers (BattlegroundMgr, RandomShadowMgr, ArenaTeamMgr) and modifies internal counters in sRandomShadowMgr for rated arenas.

doc.summary: Processes a Shadow AI bot's departure from a Battleground or Arena by updating its strategy states, logging the event, and sending a client-side leave packet.
doc.overview: This function handles the logic for a Shadow AI bot leaving a Battleground or Arena. It first verifies that the bot is currently in a valid battleground context before proceeding. The core of the function involves iterating through specific strategy tags (such as warsong, arathi, eye, and general battleground/arena states) to transition them from combat to non-combat modes, ensuring the bot's AI behavior reflects its departure.

params.name: botAI
params.desc: Pointer to the Shadow AI object representing the bot that is leaving.

doc.notes: The function logs an informational message and sends a CMSG_LEAVE_BATTLEFIELD packet to the client. It resets specific AI context values for battleground type, role, arena type, and position data upon completion.

doc.summary: Processes incoming battle ground join events for bots, parsing status data and executing logic to handle queue waiting, forced joins, or in-progress battles.
doc.overview: This function parses the event packet to extract battle ground parameters such as instance ID, map ID, level requirements, and current status. It determines the specific battleground type and arena configuration based on the bot's level and the received data, then logs relevant information for debugging. The core logic handles different statuses like waiting in a queue or an active battle, triggering actions like forced joins or automatic removal if conditions are met.

params.name: event
params.desc: The Event object containing the packet data to be parsed and processed.

doc.side_effects: Network (queues packets), Global State (accesses BattlegroundMgr, RandomShadowMgr, BotAI), Logging
doc.notes: Calls LeaveBG(botAI) if TIME_TO_AUTOREMOVE is received; handles forced joins via CMSG_BATTLEFIELD_PORT packet; relies on global managers for queue and battleground data.

doc.summary: BGJoinAction is a C++ class that enables ShadowAI bots to autonomously join battleground queues based on specific criteria.
doc.overview: This action serves as the primary mechanism for ShadowAI bots to initiate participation in Battlegrounds. It evaluates available queue types and brackets, attempting to join them if conditions are met, while also supporting gathering into arena teams when applicable. The class manages internal lists of battleground IDs to track potential targets.
doc.notes: Callers should ensure the bot has sufficient resources before execution; edge cases include queue full states or bracket restrictions.

doc.summary: Handles console commands for the Shadow system by validating configuration and session state before delegating to a private handler.
doc.overview: This function acts as a public entry point for Shadow-related console commands, first checking if the Shadow AI configuration is enabled. It then verifies that the handler has an active WorldSession, returning early with error messages if either condition fails. Finally, it delegates the actual command processing to HandleConsoleCommandPrivate and returns true upon completion.

params.name: handler
params.desc: Pointer to the ChatHandler instance that received the command.

params.name: args
params.desc: The raw string argument provided by the user in the console command.

doc.notes: Returns true on success or failure; checks for disabled Shadow system and missing active session before processing.

doc.summary: Executes GM-only console commands to summon temporary battlebot waypoints at specific battleground locations.
doc.overview: This function processes private console arguments for game masters within a battleground context, allowing them to visualize bot paths or specific entities. It validates the user's security level and current battleground state before parsing commands like 'showpath', 'showcreature', or 'showobject'. Upon successful execution, it spawns temporary creatures at calculated coordinates to represent the requested data.

params.name: session
params.desc: Pointer to the WorldSession object containing player and battleground context.

params.name: args
params.desc: String containing the command name followed by optional parameters (e.g., 'showpath=all' or 'showcreature=0').

doc.notes: Spawns temporary creatures (GUID 15631) with a 15-second despawn timer; requires GM security level and active battleground membership.

doc.summary: Retrieves the pre-configured battle strategy for a specific team within a given battleground instance.
doc.overview: This function acts as a lookup utility that maps a battleground's unique instance ID to its stored strategy configuration. It first checks if a valid strategy entry exists for the provided battleground; if not, it defaults to returning zero. Upon finding a match, it selects either the alliance or horde strategy based on the team identifier passed in.

params.name: bg
params.desc: Pointer to the Battleground object containing the instance ID used for strategy lookup.

params.name: teamId
params.desc: The team identifier (TEAM_ALLIANCE or TEAM_HORDE) determining which specific strategy variant to return.

doc.notes: Returns 0 if the battleground instance ID is not found in the global bgStrategies map. Callers should verify the returned value before applying it to bot behavior logic.

doc.summary: Executes a predefined sequence of movement and jump actions for Horde or Alliance bots to simulate tactical maneuvers on the Battleground.
doc.overview: This function retrieves the current battleground and team ID, then checks the bot's position against specific waypoints. Depending on whether the bot is part of the Horde or Alliance, it executes a distinct series of movements and jumps between coordinates until reaching the final destination in the sequence.
doc.side_effects: Movement commands (MoveTo, JumpTo) that alter bot position; potential network I/O for movement requests.
doc.notes: The function relies on precise distance checks to determine which action to perform next. It assumes the bot is already within range of the starting waypoint for its respective team.

It then verifies that the battleground status is active and the bot is alive and stationary before proceeding. The logic handles special cases such as waiting to leave, lack of combat, or line-of-sight obstructions by calculating paths and repositioning.
doc.notes: Called by the bot AI system during gameplay; edge cases include bots outside battlegrounds, dead units, or those moving between locations.
