doc.summary: Moves the bot to a designated waiting position on the current battleground based on team affiliation and role.
doc.overview: This function attempts to relocate the bot to a specific coordinate within its active battleground, utilizing predefined position constants for various battle types. It first validates that the bot has an associated battleground and checks if the force flag is set or if the battleground status allows joining; otherwise, it returns false immediately. The logic then branches based on the battleground type (such as WS, AB, AV, IC) to determine the appropriate target location, applying random offsets within a defined radius for realism.

params.name: force
params.desc: If true, allows movement regardless of the battleground's current status; if false, movement only occurs if the battleground is in STATUS_WAIT_JOIN.

doc.notes: The function relies on context values for role assignment and uses hardcoded position constants specific to different battleground maps. It handles multiple battle types including Waiting Spots, Alliance/Battlefield variants, and Ice Cavern configurations.

doc.summary: Selects a battlefield objective for the bot based on strategy, role, and current game state.
doc.overview: This function determines the target objective for a bot within an Active Warfare battleground by evaluating team roles, enemy strategies, and specific node conditions. It prioritizes mine capture or snowfall defense objectives if available, falling back to targeting nearby enemies when no other objective is set. The selection logic dynamically adjusts based on whether the bot is in offensive or defensive mode and incorporates random chance factors for role switching.

params.name: reset
params.desc: If true, forces the function to ignore existing position data and re-evaluate objectives from scratch; if false, it only selects a new objective if none currently exists.

doc.notes: The function relies on external context values for position maps and bot roles. It performs random number generation (urand) to determine mine capture targets, role switching chances, and fallback enemy targeting.

doc.summary: Moves the bot toward the objective position on the current battleground, optionally ignoring distance checks.
doc.overview: This function retrieves the objective coordinates from the game context and attempts to move the bot there. It first validates that the bot is on a valid battleground and adjusts the battleground type if necessary for specific modes like Ice Caverns. The logic then checks if the bot is already locked inside a keep or if the distance to the objective exceeds a threshold, returning false if the latter condition is met when ignoreDist is false.

params.name: ignoreDist
params.desc: If true, skips the distance check and proceeds to move toward the objective regardless of range.

doc.notes: Calls selectObjective() if position is unset; resets objective if bot reaches within 4.0f units.

doc.summary: Selects the optimal path from a provided list of BattleBotPath objects to reach the current battleground objective based on distance and reverse-path constraints.
doc.overview: This function evaluates a collection of battle paths to determine which one best leads to the active battleground objective, accounting for specific terrain rules like jump-downs or cave spawns. It calculates a composite score for each path by weighing the proximity of waypoints to the bot against their distance from the destination, adjusting these weights dynamically according to the battleground type (e.g., IC, AV, WS). The function ultimately returns true if a valid path is found and executed via moveToObjectiveWp, or false otherwise.

params.name: vPaths
params.desc: A constant reference to a vector containing pointers to BattleBotPath objects representing candidate routes.

doc.side_effects: Network (potentially via moveToObjectiveWp), Global State (modifies bot position if successful)
doc.notes: The function relies on context variables for PositionMap and battleground type; it handles specific edge cases for IC, AV, WS, and EY battlegrounds by adjusting distance scoring multipliers. If no suitable path is found after filtering out paths with disallowed reverse segments or those exceeding the bot's distance limit, it returns false.

doc.summary: Resets the battleground objective for the bot by randomly assigning a new role and position based on the specific battleground type.
doc.overview: This function initializes the bot's strategy for the current battleground by first verifying that a valid battleground exists. It then determines the probability of changing roles based on the battleground type, such as Warong or Eye of the Storm, before randomly selecting a new role and position if conditions are met. Finally, it updates the internal context with these values and triggers the objective selection logic.
doc.side_effects: Global state (modifies bot's role and position in context)
doc.notes: Depends on external functions like GetBattleground, HasAura, urand, GetValue, Set, and selectObjective. Edge case: Returns false immediately if the bot is not part of a battleground.

doc.summary: Moves the bot to a waypoint within its current path with randomized offset and handles combat or capture flag conditions.
doc.overview: This function attempts to move the battle bot toward an objective waypoint by calculating a target point based on the current position in the path. It first validates that the bot is alive, not in a state where it must stop (such as capturing a flag), and has reached the last waypoint if moving forward. The logic supports both normal progression and reverse movement along the path.

params.name: currentPath
params.desc: Pointer to the battle bot's current path containing waypoints.

params.name: currentPoint
params.desc: The index of the waypoint currently being processed in the path.

params.name: reverse
params.desc: Boolean flag indicating whether to move backward through the path instead of forward.

doc.notes: Returns false if the bot is dead, not capturing a flag while in combat, or has reached the end of the path. Randomizes the target waypoint by up to 5 steps forward or backward.

doc.summary: Determines if a battle bot can start moving toward its objective by validating path availability and distance constraints.
doc.overview: This function checks whether the bot is within range of the objective position and evaluates a list of provided paths to identify valid starting points. It filters out paths that are too close to the objective or restricted from being traversed in reverse, then randomly selects an available path to initiate movement toward the goal.

params.name: vPaths
params.desc: A constant reference to a vector containing pointers to BattleBotPath objects representing potential routes for the bot.

doc.notes: The function relies on context data for objective position and internal lists like vPaths_NoReverseAllowed; it may return false if no valid path is found or distance thresholds are not met.

doc.summary: Determines if a bot can start a new path to the objective by checking distance constraints and selecting the nearest available waypoint.
doc.overview: This function validates whether a battlebot is eligible to initiate movement toward its objective based on proximity rules and path availability. It first verifies that the battleground exists and is not an Ice Cave type, then checks if the bot is within 25 units of the objective position. If valid, it iterates through the provided vector of paths to identify the closest waypoint relative to the bot's current location.

params.name: vPaths
params.desc: A constant reference to a vector containing pointers to BattleBotPath objects representing available routes.

doc.notes: The function relies on the bot's distance calculation and context position data; it returns false if no valid path is found or if the bot is too close to the objective.

doc.summary: Determines whether a battle bot is currently occupying or attacking a specific flag object based on proximity, state, and team conditions.
doc.overview: This function evaluates the bot's position relative to game objects matching provided flag IDs within a calculated range. It first checks for enemy players nearby to determine if the bot should retreat from an objective, then verifies if friendly units are capturing the flag to decide whether to move toward it. Finally, it iterates through valid target flags to confirm occupancy or attack status.

params.name: vPaths
params.desc: A vector of BattleBotPath pointers representing potential movement paths for the bot.

params.name: vFlagIds
params.desc: A vector of unique flag IDs (uint32) that the function should consider as valid targets.

doc.notes: Calls MoveTo() to reposition the bot if a friendly unit is capturing the flag; modifies context target and resets objectives. Edge case: returns false if no valid flags are found or if an enemy player is detected within range.

doc.summary: Checks whether the flag on the current battleground has been taken by an opponent.
doc.overview: This function retrieves the active battleground instance for the bot and verifies if the flag associated with the opposing team is currently occupied. It returns true only if a valid GUID exists for the flag picker of the other team, indicating the flag is in use; otherwise, it returns false.
doc.notes: Relies on the bot's internal battleground pointer being correctly initialized. If the bot has not yet joined a battleground or the connection is unstable, the function may return false due to a null BattlegroundWS pointer.

Otherwise, the function returns false without taking any action.
doc.notes: Relies on AI_VALUE to locate the flag carrier and assumes the bot has access to map and position data via GetMapId and GetPositionX/Y/Z.

doc.summary: Returns the count of alive players within a specified distance on the battleground map, filtering by team affiliation and combat status.
doc.overview: This function queries the current battleground state to identify active players located near a specific coordinate. It first verifies that the bot is currently inside a battleground before proceeding with the search. The iteration checks each player's liveness, team alignment, and whether they are engaged in combat based on the provided flags.

params.name: teamId
params.desc: The team identifier to filter players; accepts TEAM_NEUTRAL or a specific team ID.

params.name: point
params.desc: A Position struct containing the X and Y coordinates defining the center of the search area.

params.name: range
params.desc: The maximum distance in units from the point within which players are counted.

params.name: combat
params.desc: A boolean flag; if true, excludes players currently engaged in combat from the count.

doc.notes: Returns 0 if the bot is not in a battleground or if the battleground map is null. The function relies on server-side distance calculations via sServerFacade and assumes players are stored in bg->GetBgMap()->GetPlayers().

doc.summary: Determines if the bot is inside a locked keep and attempts to use or move toward the nearest teleporter portal.
doc.overview: This function first verifies that the bot is positioned within the specific coordinates of an Icecrown Citadel (IC) battleground for either the Alliance or Horde faction. It then checks the state of the keep's portcullis gate; if locked, it searches for the closest active teleporter portal among nearby game objects. Finally, it attempts to interact with the portal using a server opcode if within range, otherwise moves the bot directly to the portal's location.
doc.notes: Relies on server-side distance calculations and game object states; may trigger movement or network calls depending on portal availability.

It utilizes std::find_if to locate the first non-whitespace character and then erases all preceding elements up to that point, modifying the original string directly without creating a copy.

params.name: s
params.desc: A reference to a std::string whose leading whitespace will be removed.

doc.side_effects: Modifies the input string in-place; performs no I/O or network operations.
doc.notes: Caller must ensure 's' is not empty before calling, as erase on an empty range is valid but erasing from begin to find_if (which returns begin) results in an empty string. Edge case: if the string contains only whitespace, it becomes empty.
